blocks.text: Bridging Functional Medicine and Emotional Well-Being

Dr. Hartman has been a functional medicine practitioner for nearly 16 years, pioneering integrative healthcare at her wellness center, Therapeutic Health. She emphasized the importance of addressing not just physical symptoms but also underlying emotional stressors that contribute to chronic health issues.

“When you look at the gut-brain axis and neuroinflammatory problems that stem from lifestyle, diet, and stress, it becomes clear that emotional health is foundational to overall well-being,” said Dr. Hartman.

Functional medicine focuses on treating root causes rather than symptoms, and NET aligns seamlessly with this approach by addressing stored emotional stress that affects both mental and physical health.
What is Neuro Emotional Technique?

Neuro Emotional Technique (NET) is a muscle-testing method used to identify and resolve emotional blockages stored in the body. It operates on the premise that past emotional experiences can become trapped in the nervous system, influencing present-day reactions to stress.

“No matter how balanced your hormones are, how fit you are, or how good your diet is, if your body is interpreting present-day stress through the lens of past trauma, it will impact your health,” explained Dr. Hartman.

NET helps individuals recognize these subconscious emotional triggers, offering a way to neutralize their impact. McAdams likened it to putting on an “emotional wetsuit” — a way to maintain emotional equilibrium without suppressing feelings.
Breaking Down Emotional Conditioning

McAdams highlighted how past conditioning affects emotional responses. “We live in a state of reactivity or avoidance, filtering our experiences through the meaning-making matrix developed in childhood. NET brings these subconscious patterns to the surface, allowing us to navigate them consciously.”

For many, emotions are deeply tied to early experiences with family and societal expectations. McAdams pointed out that women, in particular, are often conditioned to “produce, perfect, and perform,” leading to chronic stress and burnout. NET helps individuals recognize these patterns and reclaim control over their emotional responses.
A Practical Example: How NET Works

To demonstrate, Dr. Hartman performed a muscle test on McAdams, revealing an unresolved emotional stressor linked to family relationships. By identifying the emotional imprint and its source, NET provides a pathway for releasing stored stress, ultimately reducing its physiological impact.

Dr. Hartman shared a real-world application: “I recently worked with a mother struggling with the way her teenage daughter treated her. Until that dynamic changes, she has to find a way to navigate it. NET helped her neutralize the emotional charge to communicate more effectively, rather than reacting from a place of distress.”
Why Emotional Regulation Matters

Nowadays, external stressors are inevitable. However, as McAdams pointed out, “We can’t always create safety outside of ourselves, but we can create safety internally. When we do, we gain agency over our responses, rather than feeling at the mercy of our environment.”
NET empowers individuals to:

items: Strengthen relationships by responding rather than reacting
Gain clarity on past emotional triggers and neutralize their influence

blocks.text: As scientific research on NET continues to grow, with over 34 published studies validating its effectiveness, it is becoming an indispensable tool for those seeking to optimize mental and physical health.
Conclusion

True wellness isn’t just about nutrition, exercise, or even medical treatment. It’s about integrating health’s emotional, mental, and physical aspects. As Dr. Hartman put it, “NET isn’t about making emotions disappear — it’s about giving people the ability to process them in a way that supports their well-being.”
For those looking to holistically take charge of their health, NET offers a powerful bridge between the mind and body, unlocking new levels of emotional freedom and resilience.
